Deepak Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January,
2025
Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:586
 1 Mcrc-4
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani

On The 10 th Of January, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 488 of 2025
 Deepak Sharma
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Vibhor Kumar Sahu - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Harish Sharma - Public Prosecutor for the State.
 Order

1. This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS (439 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of bail relating to Crime No.88/2024 registered at Police Station Cyber Cell Hi-Tech Offence,
District Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 420, 204, 120-B, 34 of IPC and Sections 43-A,
66, 66-D of the Information Technology Adhiniyam.

District Gwalior
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. As per prosecution case, an amount of Rs.31,67,000/- has been defrauded by the co-accused from the complainant.
Allegation against the applicant is that he used to withdraw the amount through ATM of co-accused and provide the same to the co-accused on commission basis.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
He is in custody since 06.12.2024.

As per the story of prosecution, applicant has withdrawn amount from the bank account of co-accused Arun through ATM of Arun, but as per the story of prosecution total fraud Signature has been Not Verified committed in respect of Rs.31,67,000/-, whereas as per the Signed by: MADHU prosecution itself there was more than Rs.32 lac in the bank account of Arun and SOODAN PRASAD Signing time: 10-01-2025 06:02:33 PM NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:586 2 MCRC-488-2025 Rs.7,49,000/- in the bank account of co-accused Rishabh.
Therefore, whatever amount revealed as defrauded, more than that amount is deposited in the bank account of co-accused Arun and Rishabh.
Mere seizure of Rs.5,000/-, ATM card of Arun and mobile phone do not indicate that present applicant is anyhow related with the offence.
He is innocent and falsely implicated in the case.
One more case is registered against present applicant, but that is under minor offence.
He is ready and willing to abide by all the terms and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.

On these grounds,
learned counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the bail application and prayed to dismiss the bail application.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and attending facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed, but with certain stringent conditions and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-(Rupees One Lac Only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court.
In case, if he is found involved in the offence of same nature, this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically without further reference to the Bench.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE ms/-
